contentHtml:
Sept 22 (Reuters) - Viking Therapeutics

(VKTX.O), opens new tab

on Tuesday said patients shifted to a less frequent dosing regimen of its experimental obesity treatment showed superior ​weight-loss maintenance in a study compared with those on placebo.

Shares ‌of the drug developer closed 35.7% higher at $40.85, marking their biggest one-day percentage gain in more than two years.

Sign up here.

The results support the company's bid to make treatment less burdensome. Viking has ​been working on flexible dosing options with injectable and oral versions ​of VK2735 in an effort to carve out a place ⁠for itself in the fast-growing sector.

The company said on Tuesday that patients who ​switched to an every-other-week dosing of VK2735 maintained up to 97% of the ​weight they had lost during an initial 21-week treatment period, while those on a monthly dosing retained up to 90% of their prior weight loss over the following 12 ​weeks.

Louis Aronne, a former president of the Obesity Society, said less frequent dosing ​could help patients stay on obesity medicines longer.

The obesity market is currently dominated by treatments ‌from ⁠pharma majors Novo Nordisk

(NOVOb.CO), opens new tab

and Eli Lilly

(LLY.N), opens new tab

, which are locked in a battle for market share through effective and convenient treatments including injections and pills.

Analysts expect the obesity market to reach $100 billion in annual sales by 2030.

Leerink Partners analyst ​Thomas Smith said the ​data reinforces VK2735's ⁠differentiated profile and competitive positioning, and described the drug's safety and tolerability profile as "impressively clean."

In a small group treated ​weekly for 33 weeks, patients lost an average of 21.7% ​of body ⁠weight, Viking said, adding that it plans to study oral maintenance dosing later in the trial.

"We believe long-term weight management will not follow a standard one-size-fits-all ⁠approach," Viking ​CEO Brian Lian said, adding that patients ​will need a range of options to personalize treatment throughout their weight-loss journey.

Reporting by Padmanabhan Ananthan in ​Bengaluru; additional reporting by Kamal Choudhury; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli and Jonathan Ananda
